subject: botany
question_text: What does 'S' refer to in the 70S and 80S ribosome?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 9 'The Unit of Life' (book pp.23-26), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star rank and NO year citations - so stars are 0 and appearances are empty by fact, not by omission. Only ONE source book is held for botany: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus. The two-book union check and the back-test are therefore STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely unrun - never read this as 'checked and clean'. The mark split is this card's claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. BOOK GAP: the book defines S as an 'indirect measure of density and size of ribosome' and omits both shape and the fact that S values are not additive. This card writes the standard definition (sedimentation coefficient) and keeps the book's 'indirect measure' phrasing inside it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The unit
lines: It is the sedimentation coefficient of a
particle — how fast the particle settles
when it is spun in an ultracentrifuge.
steps.why: S is not a unit of mass or of length. It is a rate of settling, which is why the answer has to name the ultracentrifuge.
common_mistakes: Writing that S stands for size. It stands for Svedberg.
Calling S a unit of mass or of weight.
steps.memory_tip: S for Svedberg, who built the ultracentrifuge. S measures settling.
steps.margin_note: Naming the Svedberg unit carries this mark.

steps.label: What it measures
lines: Settling rate depends on size, shape and
density, so S is an indirect measure of the
That is why the 70S prokaryotic ribosome is
made of a 50S and a 30S subunit, and the 80S
eukaryotic ribosome of a 60S and a 40S.
steps.why: Because S measures a rate and not an amount, two subunits joined together do not give the sum of their S values — the joined particle has a different shape. The book's answer says only 'indirect measure of density and size'; shape counts too.
common_mistakes: Writing 50S + 30S = 80S. The values do not add.
Saying S measures only density. Shape and size count as well.
steps.memory_tip: 70 = 50 + 30 is bad arithmetic but good biology, because S is a rate, not an amount.
steps.margin_note: The 70S and 80S split is the line examiners look for.

insider_note: The book answers this in one line. Adding shape, and the 50S + 30S example, is what turns it into a full 2-mark answer.
